To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the knockdown of the RNAi pathway genes Ago1, Ago1, Dcr1 or Drosha in western corn root worms resulted in reduced survival and ovoposition rate, and that the knockdown or loss of function for RNAi pathway genes may confer resistance to RNAi-based insect pest control methods.
Ago1 plays a critical role in the fitness of adult WCR and that Ago1 is essential for the survival of adult insects.
the knockdown of the Argonautes Ago2 and Ago1 genes and Dicer genes Dcr2 and Dcr1 in western corn root worm (WCR) adults had different fitness consequences.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and functional characterization of RNAi pathway components in WCR and the potential impacts of the knockdown of these genes on insect fitness.
the identification of the RNAi pathway in WCR and the functional characterization of RNAi pathway components in WCR.
the identification and characterization of the Argonautes and Dicers that regulate miRNA and/or dsRNA-mediated gene silencing pathways in WCR.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the downregulation of RNAi pathway gene expression may confer resistance to RNAi-based control strategies.
RNAi-mediated pest control strategies should be carefully evaluated in terms of their potential impacts on the fitness of target species.
RNAi pathway genes may be targeted for pest control purposes, but only after a careful assessment of the potential fitness costs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the RNAi pathway is critical to WCR adult survival, and thus, it is essential for the successful development of RNAi based pest control methods.
Ago1 is an essential gene for WCR adult survival, and Ago1 is a potential target for the development of RNAi-based control measures for WCR.
the RNAi pathway genes are not all equal in their roles in the fitness of insects.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the knockdown of genes that play a key role in the insect RNAi pathway can result in significant fitness costs, which can be exploited to control insect pests.
the fitness cost associated with the knock-down of Ago1 may be used as a potential strategy to control WCR adults.
the fitness cost associated with the knock-down of RNAi pathway gene(s) needs to be evaluated in order to develop pest control strategies that rely on RNAi.
